result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_newman_watts_strogatz_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a Newman-Watts-Strogatz small-world graph: a ring lattice plus random shortcuts. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L9870-L9979){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_newman_watts_strogatz_graph( n, k, p, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Newman-Watts-Strogatz graph](/assets/graphs/add-newman-watts-strogatz-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three Newman-Watts-Strogatz graphs on a ring of eight nodes with k=2 and shortcut probability p=0, 0.3, and 0.6. The ring is never broken: accent-colored shortcuts are added on top of it, 1 at p=0.3 and 4 at p=0.6, instead of replacing ring edges as in the Watts-Strogatz model." width="100%"} Arranges `n` nodes in a ring and joins each to its `k // 2` nearest neighbors on either side (so an odd `k` rounds down). Then, for each lattice edge `(u, v)`, with probability `p` a shortcut is added from `u` to a node chosen uniformly among those not already adjacent to it. Unlike `add_smallworld_graph()`, which moves lattice edges, this keeps every lattice edge and only adds shortcuts, so for `k >= 2` the graph is always connected. With `k < n` the lattice has `n * (k // 2)` edges, and about a fraction `p` of that number again is added as shortcuts; `k == n` gives the complete graph. The process follows NetworkX's `newman_watts_strogatz_graph()`. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Newman-Watts-Strogatz graphs are useful for: - small-world experiments that shouldn't be confounded by the graph breaking apart - studying how a few shortcuts shrink path lengths while clustering stays high - analytic work, since the model is easier to treat than Watts-Strogatz rewiring ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Each node is joined to its `k // 2` nearest neighbors on each side of the ring. Must be at most `n=`. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of adding a shortcut for each lattice edge, between `0` and `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` or `k=` is negative, `k=` is greater than `n=`, or `p=` is not between `0` and `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The lattice of `30` nodes with `k=4` has `30 * 2 = 60` edges, and the shortcuts come on top of them: ::: {#4c5f00d7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_newman_watts_strogatz_graph(n=30, k=4, p=0.2, seed=3) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (30, 68) ``` ::: ::: Adding shortcuts never disconnects the ring, but it does shrink the diameter: ::: {#2c53d322 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ ( p, ec.Graph() .add_newman_watts_strogatz_graph(n=60, k=4, p=p, seed=3) .get_diameter(), ) for p in (0.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [(0.0, 15), (0.05, 8), (0.2, 6), (0.5, 5)] ``` ::: :::
